cr.tip.ignoreAtari: 💡 When stones are in atari (one liberty), first check whether they can escape or can be given up.
cr.tip.selfAtari: 💡 Before playing, count how many liberties your stones will have.
cr.tip.missCapture: 💡 Count the liberties of the opponent's stones to spot captures.
cr.tip.urgent: 💡 "Urgent points before big points": weak groups and cutting points come first.
cr.tip.bigPoint: 💡 Corners, then sides, then the centre. Wide open areas are worth the most.
cr.tip.endgame: 💡 In the endgame play sente moves first, then the biggest ones.
cr.tip.pass: 💡 Pass only when there is nothing left worth playing.
cr.tip.gen: 💡 Look at the whole board and ask where the biggest point is.
cr.nav: Use ◀ ▶ to see the comment for each move.
intro.hist: Go was born in ancient China and reached Japan by the 8th century. In the Edo period the shogunate supported Go houses such as Hon'inbō. Today Go is played all over the world, and in 2016 an AI beat a top professional, a famous moment for AI.
intro.win: Black and White take turns placing stones on the intersections of the lines. Players surround areas of the board (territory); at the end, the larger territory wins. Stones that are completely surrounded are captured.
intro.cult: Many Japanese words come from Go, such as dame ("no good") and ichimoku oku ("to give someone a stone" = to respect). Reviewing the game together afterwards is a cherished Go tradition.
tr.place.b:
Black plays first, then each player places one stone in turn.
Stones go on the intersections of the lines, not inside the squares.
tr.place.task: Place a black stone on any intersection.
tr.place.ok: That is a move in Go!
tr.capture.b:
The empty points next to a stone (up, down, left, right) are its liberties.
Fill all of them and the stone is captured.
tr.capture.task: Play on the white stone's last liberty to capture it.
tr.capture.ok: Captured! Captured stones are your prisoners.
tr.group.b:
Stones connected up, down, left or right form one group.
They share their liberties and are captured together.
tr.group.task: Fill the last liberty of the two white stones to capture both.
tr.escape.b:
A stone with only one liberty is in atari.
Extend it to gain liberties and it is safe for now.
tr.escape.task: Extend the black stone in atari to escape.
tr.escape.ng: Extend in the direction that gives more liberties.
tr.suicide.b:
You may not play where your stone would have no liberties.
But if the move captures an opponent's stone, it is allowed.
tr.suicide.task: Play inside White's shape to capture a white stone.
tr.suicide.no: You cannot play there. Find the point that captures.
tr.suicide.ok: Captured! A capturing move is allowed even when surrounded.
tr.ko.b:
White has just captured a black stone. Taking back at once would repeat the same shape forever.
So you must play elsewhere once before retaking (the ko rule).
tr.ko.task: Play elsewhere first; after White answers, retake.
tr.ko.no: Ko: you cannot retake at once. Play elsewhere first.
tr.ko.now: White played elsewhere. Now you may retake!
tr.ko.ok: Retaken! That is the ko rule.
tr.terr.b:
Empty points surrounded by your stones are your territory.
At the end, the player with more territory wins.
tr.terr.task: Who has more territory? Tap that colour's stones or area.
tr.terr.ok: Right! Black {b}, White {w}: White has more.
tr.terr.ng: Count again: Black {b}, White {w}. White has more.
tr.end.b:
When there is nothing useful left to play, you pass. Two passes in a row end the game.
Dead stones (×) are removed, then territory and prisoners are counted. White, who played second, gets komi (e.g. 6.5 points).
